finding.title: Fix unsafe `as int?`/`as num?` casts in TrackCodec.decode and GoalCodec.decode that throw instead of returning null
finding.rule: EH-2/EH-4 decode() null-on-malformed contract + Nygard partial-failure
finding.why: entity_codec.dart's decode() contract states it 'Returns null when required fields are missing or malformed — the merger must skip malformed rows rather than crash.' Every other numeric field read across all 15 files in this batch goes through FirestoreCodec.parseInt, built specifically because Firestore fields can arrive as String (its own docstring says so). These 3 sites bypass it with a bare `as` cast: if profile_id/track_id/target_percent ever arrives as anything but exactly int (or num, for target_percent)/null — e.g. a String from a hand-edited doc, an import script, or a legacy document — `as int?`/`as num?` throws instead of returning null. TrackConfigMerger.merge() and GoalMerger.merge() call `_codec.decode(row)` inside a `for` loop with no try/catch, and MergeRouter.dispatch (merge_router.dart:55) awaits merger.merge() with no try/catch either, so one malformed row throws out of the whole pull page mid-iteration, silently dropping every row after it and aborting the sync pass instead of just skipping the bad row.
finding.recommendation: Replace `raw['profile_id'] as int?` / `raw['track_id'] as int?` with `FirestoreCodec.parseInt(raw['profile_id'])` / `FirestoreCodec.parseInt(raw['track_id'])` (the int.tryParse fallback lines become redundant and can be deleted). Add a `FirestoreCodec.parseDouble` helper mirroring parseInt and use it for GoalCodec's target_percent instead of the raw `as num?` cast.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: TrackCodec().decode({'profile_id': '5', 'track_id': '7', 'curriculum_id': 'x', 'activated_at': <iso>}) returns a TrackRow, not a thrown exception.
Unit test: GoalCodec().decode({...,'target_percent': '55'}) returns a GoalRow with targetPercent 55.0 instead of throwing.
grep for 'as int?' / 'as num?' / 'as double?' / 'as bool?' across lib/core/sync/codec/*.dart returns zero matches (wire into make audit).
